result.experiment: E7: move headword (canonical form) proposals to intake so click-time grammar never waits on a sequential Luna call. After analyzeSentence, one Luna call per sentence (strict json_schema, cached system prompt built from the production canonicalFormGuidance plus citation-shape rules) proposes the headword for every listed Lexeme target (all except DET/AUX/PRON) and every named Phraseme target. At click time, arm H appends the proposal for the clicked target to canonicalFormAlternatives and adds E2's VERB infinitive-shape guard and Idiom/Collocation phraseme guard. BASE is unmodified src. Live coverage: a held-out set of 54 strong/irregular VERB sentences (BASE x2, H x2, interleaved) and the VERB corpus (fresh BASE x1, H x1, plus E2's 2 archived same-src BASE reps). Midway the TypeSafe account returned HTTP 402 (no credits), so the live ADJ/Idiom click-time runs could not execute. Those routes are covered offline instead, from E2 records made on the same src (request-identical H replay, and a counterfactual F), using oracle-target proposals.

result.caseLevelDiff:
Held-out (54 cases, 2 reps each arm):
- Base-vs-base noise is 8 canonical flips and 3 status flips; H-vs-H is 2 and 2.
- BASE -> H, paired by case-rep: canonical false->true 26, true->false 0.
- Per case: 9 consistent gains (kroch, entschied sich, widersprach, mied, zog an, schlug vor, verhielt sich, benahmen sich, unterhielten sich), 0 consistent losses. 8 mixed cases all favour H (base 1/2 vs H 2/2: wog, maß, tritt, wurde gestohlen, fiel aus, trat zurück, verließ sich auf; hinterließ 0/2 vs 1/2). No case is worse under H.

| Group | BASE | H |
|---|---|---|
| E2 skeptic probe (10 verbs) | 15/20 correct, 1 wrong | 19/20, 0 wrong |
| strong preterite | 32/44 | 39/44 |
| present | 5/6 | 6/6 |
| aux+participle | 11/12 | 12/12 |
| separable | 4/14 | 10/14 |
| reflexive | 5/12 | 12/12 |

For comparison, E2's rule candidates on the probe were 1/10 right and 7/10 wrong. The 4 separable misses in H are sah|ein and nahmen|teil: the analysis split each verb into two VERB targets, so there was no proposal.

VERB corpus (77 cases):
- Fresh BASE -> H: pass +21/-0, canonical +22/-0, against base-vs-base noise of 5-7 pass and 5-9 canonical flips.
- Against all 3 BASE reps: 17 consistent gains (Lauf, hinauszulaufen, erinnert sich an, steht auf, mag, kann, wird, hat, sehnen sich nach, erholt sich, darf, sol, könen, contrast mag, sind, bekommt geliefert, bekommt geöffnet), 0 consistent losses, 10 mixed all favouring H.
- H introduced 0 wrong lemmas. Its one wrong lemma (werden for wird ... finden) had no proposal and is 0/3 in BASE.
- Hreplay adds 94 samples with 0 wrong lemmas, +24/-0 canonical and +25/-2 pass (both losses 'Sei', other field).

Presence-bias risk table: every case where the proposal is wrong or null, checked against archived production.
- Wrong proposals follow a different convention from the corpus: NOUN suspended compounds (Kinder- -> Kind, gold Kinderbuch; 4 cases), a licensed variant (Photographie, gold Fotografie), abbreviations kept instead of expanded (Dipl.-Ing., ca., z.B., usw. x2, u. a., o.Ä., v.a.), 'oder … Ähnliches', and Collocation 'Hilfe in Anspruch nehmen' (added a free object).
- Idiom: 'was zum' (truncated partial idiom).
- In every one of these, production is also wrong or Unresolved, so 0 would newly break a correct production result.
- Null proposals (2) are not offered, so they are harmless.
findings: Precision holds out of sample, so the rule-candidate failure does not recur. On the 54 held-out strong/irregular, inseparable, separable and reflexive verbs, all 52 matched intake proposals equal gold. That includes all 10 of E2's skeptic probe verbs, where E2's rule candidates produced 7 pseudo-infinitives (schworen, stanken, ...). VERB corpus: 62/62 matched proposals correct, and 61/61 on an independent second sample. ADJ with oracle targets: 32/32. Luna-generated candidates keep the precision of today's Luna fallback without the out-of-table failure.

Presence bias works in our favour when the candidate is right. jev picked the offered proposal every time the op reached the canonical step: 156/156 live (held-out 100/100, VERB 56/56). So lemma accuracy becomes proposal accuracy. Held-out canonical: 72/108 -> 98/108, with 17 wrong lemmas -> 0. VERB corpus: pass 43 -> 64/77, canonical 48 -> 70/77. Neither set has a consistent loss; base-vs-base noise is 8 (held-out) and 5-9 (VERB) canonical flips.

BASE's wrong lemmas are mostly jev accepting the inflected joined text: 16 of 108 held-out ops (zog an, verhielt sich, tritt, wog, maß, ...). Click-time Luna also erred ('sich auf jemanden verlassen'). The proposal removes both. The VERB infinitive guard fired 0 times when a proposal was present and 2 times on unmatched cases (sehnen sich nach, warnen vor), both fixed via Luna. Without the guards (H0), VERB canonical drops from 70 to 68.

The click-time Luna call goes away where a proposal exists. Luna follow-up: held-out 74% -> 1.9%, VERB corpus 60% -> 14%, and the remaining 14% is only the 15 corpus cases the analysis grouped differently. Grammar p50: held-out 1396 -> 360 ms (paired median -985 ms), VERB corpus 1225 -> 322 ms (paired median -439, mean -501 ms). p90: held-out 1719-1919 -> 444-489 ms, VERB corpus 1617 -> 1291 ms (still dominated by unmatched cases). Cost per click: $0.00034-0.00036 -> $0.00024-0.00027.

Intake-time cost. The headword call runs sequentially after analyzeSentence. It adds p50 1450-1615 ms and p90 1949-2781 ms (max 8.4 s) of background time, so a proposal is ready about 1.9-2.1 s (p50) and 2.5-3.4 s (p90) after the sentence is accepted. A click earlier than that falls back to today's path. It also adds $0.00021-0.00028 per ingested sentence, whether or not anything is clicked (+22-31% over analyzeSentence alone). Output tokens drive the cost: 50-72 at $2.40/M.

The promptsmith executor sends json_schema strict:false. With a nested headwords array, 11/54 responses (20%) dropped the {value} wrapper and came back as undefined. The strict executor (luna-strict.ts) was valid 380/380. Proposals were otherwise stable: 142/143 targets identical across the two executors on the same analyses.

Match rate is 52/54 on held-out and 62/77 on the VERB corpus. Misses: the analysis split a separable verb into two VERB targets (sah|ein, nahmen|teil, wirken|nach as ADV); a governed preposition became a separate ADP (wartet|auf, warten|auf, warnen|vor, wurde|um|gebeten); AUX+participle split (ist|geschlossen as AUX+ADJ, wird|finden, hätt|bestellt); and long DW sentences. In production the click target is the analysis target, so every analysed target gets a proposal. The misses measure corpus-vs-analysis membership disagreement, not coverage. Disclosure: before any grammar run I fixed two of my own held-out memberships to include the governed preposition, following the corpus convention; golds unchanged.

E4 exact-match acceptance, i.e. how often the proposal equals the final canonicalForm. Under H: held-out 96/104 ops with a proposal (92%, 98% of Success ops), VERB corpus 60/62 (97%), VERB replay 92/94, ADJ replay 21/23 (91%). With the proposal only used as an emoji guess and grammar unchanged: held-out 67%, VERB 66%, ADJ 72%, Idiom 21%. Idiom rises to 79% under F. So the intake proposal is a much better speculative-emoji key than E4's rule guess, but mainly once grammar consumes it.

ADJ and phrasemes are covered offline only: jev returned HTTP 402 for every call from 08:45Z, $0 spent. ADJ H replay (23 request-identical E2 records): 21/21 correct, +2/-0 canonical, Luna 48% -> 0, paired p50 -246 ms. Idiom oracle proposals are 25/27 correct in corpus notation. The F counterfactual on 2 archived base reps, with the phraseme guard and the proposal, gives canonical 12 -> 42/54 (0 wrong), pass 8 -> 26 (+18/-0), Luna 20% -> 4%, estimated p50 ~353 ms (guard alone: 1215 ms). None of this used analyzeSentence targets, so phraseme match rate and H behaviour are unmeasured.

Off the VERB/ADJ routes the prompt does not yet match the corpus conventions. Oracle proposals: NOUN 37/44 (suspended compounds, a licensed variant, abbreviation expansion), ADV 40/49 (8 abbreviations not expanded, plus 'oder … Ähnliches'), Collocation 12/13 (added a free object). On unscored targets there are odd NUM outputs (Fünftel -> 5, ersten -> 1. or eins) and nominalized-adjective drift between samples. None of the wrong proposals is on a case production gets right today, but under presence bias a wrong proposal could turn an honest Unresolved into a persisted wrong Lemma. That was not measured live.

Side effects of changing canonicalFormAlternatives on other answers match E2. Unresolved fell (held-out 18 -> 10, VERB 9 -> 6). There were 2 other-field pass losses, both in replay records only ('Sei' person, 2 samples; the live H passed it), plus 'glänzend' on ADJ. The live H runs had 0 pass losses.

result.expectedProductionImpact:
VERB clicks with a ready proposal:
- Grammar p50 drops from ~1.2-1.4 s to ~0.33-0.36 s, and p90 from ~1.6-1.9 s to ~0.45-0.5 s. Paired median saving is ~440 ms on the corpus (where 20% of cases lacked a proposal) and ~985 ms on held-out strong verbs.
- The click-time Luna canonical call goes from 60-74% of VERB clicks to ~0-2%.
- Wrong VERB lemmas go from 8-9 per 54 strong-verb clicks to 0. Inflected forms persisted as headwords (zog an, verhielt sich, tritt) are eliminated, and corpus contract pass rises from ~56% to ~83%.
- Click cost drops ~$0.0001.

Intake:
- One extra background Luna call per sentence: +$0.00021-0.00028 per sentence regardless of clicks, and +1.45-1.6 s p50 / 1.9-2.8 s p90 before proposals are ready (max seen 8.4 s). Clicks inside that window get today's latency.
- Offline evidence suggests similar gains on ADJ (Luna 44-48% -> 0, 3 wrong lemmas fixed) and Idiom (canonical 22% -> 78%, Luna 20% -> 4%), but neither was measured live with analysis targets.
result.risks:
1. Presence bias. Once a proposal is offered, jev picked it 156/156 times, so proposal accuracy is lemma accuracy on every route where proposals are offered. VERB/ADJ precision was 100% on 52+62+61+32 matched samples, but the held-out set is 54 sentences I wrote. Rare verbs, dialect, typos and long real-world sentences may be worse. NOUN/ADV/NUM proposals already violate corpus conventions (abbreviations, suspended compounds, variants, numerals). There, a wrong proposal could turn an Unresolved into a persisted wrong Lemma, which then feeds lemmaCandidates for later clicks.
2. Incomplete live coverage. jev ran out of credits (HTTP 402) at 08:45Z, so there are no live H runs on ADJ, Idiom, Collocation, NOUN or ADV. ADJ rests on 23 request-identical replay records from E2 (taken 2 h earlier). Idiom rests on an offline counterfactual with oracle targets. The analysis may not produce matching phraseme targets: E1 saw phraseme clicks fail the support gate.
3. Thin reps. The VERB corpus has 1 fresh H rep and 1 fresh BASE rep. Noise comes from E2's archived same-src base reps and 94 replay samples. The held-out set has 2x2.
4. Timing. A proposal is ready only ~2 s p50 / ~3.4 s p90 after sentence intake, with an 8.4 s tail. I did not measure how often learners click sooner. Running the call in parallel with analyzeSentence would need word-level proposals and could mismatch membership.
5. Executor. promptsmith strict:false silently drops ~20% of these nested answers; this needs strict mode or a schema change.
6. Side effects. The extra alternative also moves unrelated jev answers: fewer Unresolved here, and a flaky imperative person on 'Sei' in replay. That is small but real.
7. Cost is paid for every ingested sentence, clicked or not; output tokens are the cost driver.
8. Intake nondeterminism. 7/423 targets changed between samples, all on unscored non-VERB targets.

My probe (skeptic-summary.json):
- VERB proposal precision: 59/62 = 95.2%, Wilson 95% CI 86.7-98.3%.
- Errors, each reproduced identically in a second sample:
  - 'Der Bäcker wog das Mehl genau ab' -> abwägen (gold abwiegen; arguable, since Duden marks the weighing sense of abwägen as outdated).
  - 'Wenn ich Zeit hätte, führe ich gern mit' -> mitführen (gold mitfahren).
  - 'Wenn es nicht so teuer wäre, führen wir ... nach Italien' -> führen (gold fahren).
- Controls (führte -> führen, gemalt -> malen, hing -> hängen) were all right.
- Pooled out-of-sample VERB precision (E7 held-out plus mine): 111/114 = 97.4%, CI 92.5-99.1%.
- E7's own held-out 0/52 errors only bounds precision at >=93.1% (95% confidence). It never established 100%.
problems: Precision is not 100% out of sample. On harder sentences E7 never saw, the intake call proposed wrong real-word homographs 3 times in 62 VERB targets: mitführen for Konjunktiv II führe+mit (should be mitfahren), führen for Konjunktiv II führen (should be fahren), and abwägen for Mehl abwiegen. All 3 reproduced in a second sample, so they are systematic, not noise. They are infinitive-shaped, so E2's VERB guard passes them.

jev does not check the proposal. E7 saw 156/156 picks, and the E2 skeptic's archived live probe shows jev also took nonsense candidates whenever one was offered and the op reached the canonical step (schworen, stanken, schmolzen, stachen, schlichen, bliesen, sich entschieden). So under H, a wrong proposal like 'mitführen' (which differs from the joined text 'führe mit') would almost certainly be stored as a wrong Lemma, and would then feed lemmaCandidates for later clicks. I could not measure this live (jev HTTP 402), and I could not measure whether BASE would make the same mistake.

The accuracy gain is attributed to the wrong change. The relevant counterfactual is BASE plus E2's VERB guard, which the recommendation ships anyway, not bare BASE. E7's own F trace shows 16 held-out BASE ops where jev accepted non-infinitive joined text. That is 16 of the 17 wrong lemmas, and the guard alone (with the Luna fallback) would catch them; the 17th was a Luna error. So most of '17 wrong -> 0' and much of the VERB corpus canonical gain would come from the guard. The unique value of intake proposals is latency (no Luna on the click path) and fewer Unresolved (18 -> 10), not lemma accuracy.

The rules are tuned to the VERB corpus. The prompt's examples avoid corpus verbs; I checked, and only 'vorbei' appears, in the unevaluated ADP and PART corpora. But the added VERB rules encode the corpus's own conventions: recipient-passive bekommen/kriegen/erhalten (corpus cases bekommt+geliefert and erhielt+überreicht), 'a modal is its own headword' (many modal cases), 'correct an evident misspelling' (könen, sol, mus, tanzd), and the sentence-initial lowercasing rule (Lauf). So the VERB corpus result (62/62, 17 consistent gains including bekommt geliefert, mag, kann, darf, sol, könen) is in-sample for the rule set. My out-of-sample kriegen+geschenkt case did pass.

The held-out set is easy. Its 54 short textbook sentences were written by the same person who wrote the prompt, and most test strong-verb stem mapping, which LLMs do well. It has no homographs, Konjunktiv II, colloquial forms or long sentences. It also includes a post-hoc membership edit (2 cases) made after the first intake run showed the analysis grouping. That edit only raises the match rate from 50 to 52 of 54, but the edit time is 08:39Z, between the s1 and s1b runs.

Wrong proposals on split targets are not counted. Match-rate misses are called 'membership disagreement, not coverage', but in production the click carries the proposal for the analysis target, and on unmatched targets E7's own records contain wrong proposals nobody scored: 'nahmen [Head]' -> nehmen (the lexical verb is teilnehmen, and 'teil' got teilnehmen), 'Modalverb [Head]' on the VERB route -> 'modalverb' (lowercased), 'zu [Head]' as VERB -> 'zu', and 'erhielt [Head]' in a recipient passive -> erhalten. Split heads are also unstable: 'sah [Head]' gave einsehen with the strict executor and sehen with promptsmith. And the 15 unmatched VERB-corpus cases ran H with no proposal, a condition that does not exist in production.

Factual error in the case-level diff: 'The 4 separable misses in H are sah|ein and nahmen|teil' is wrong. nahmen-teil was 2/2 correct in H (via Luna). The misses are sah-ein (no proposal, Unresolved at support) and hat-angenommen, where the proposal 'annehmen' was picked but both H reps ended Unresolved at hasSepPrefix.

The E4 acceptance numbers under H are circular. Under H, jev chooses the final canonicalForm from the offered proposal, so 'proposal equals final canonicalForm' is about 98% of Success ops by construction. It measures proposal accuracy only where the proposal is right. Using one Luna call as both the speculative emoji key and, through presence bias, the lemma also removes the independent cross-check: when the proposal is wrong, emoji and Lemma will be consistently wrong together.

The cost claim is one-sided. The click saves about $0.0001, but intake adds $0.00021-0.00028 per ingested sentence, clicked or not. Net cost goes down only with about 2-3 or more VERB clicks per sentence, which is not measured. The recommended VERB-only route also pays output tokens for proposals on all 3.3-5.5 listed targets per sentence.
Minor count errors: the strict-validity count is 382/382, not 380/380, and the luna-strict.ts comment says 12/54 promptsmith failures where the actual count is 11/54.

ADJ, Idiom and Collocation rest only on offline evidence: request-identical replay from E2 arm A, a subset biased toward cases where E2's rule candidate equalled the proposal, and an F counterfactual with oracle targets. The report says so openly, but F keeps jev's answers unchanged, whereas H changes jev's canonical question and would take whatever proposal is offered. Neither live H behaviour nor the phraseme match rate against analysis targets is measured.
claimsThatHold: The recomputed live numbers match the raw records: held-out canonical 72/108 -> 98/108, VERB corpus pass 43 -> 64 and canonical 48 -> 70, and the Luna rates, latency percentiles, paired deltas and costs.

Relative to bare BASE the direction is clear and well beyond noise: held-out +26/-0 case-reps against 8 base-vs-base canonical flips, VERB corpus +22/-0 against 5-9 flips, and no case is worse under H.
When a proposal is offered, jev picks it essentially every time (156/156 live). Lemma accuracy therefore equals proposal accuracy.

Where a correct proposal exists, the click-time Luna canonical call goes away. VERB grammar p50 drops to about 320-360 ms, and the paired median saving is about 985 ms on held-out and 439 ms on the corpus.
promptsmith's strict:false setting silently drops about 20% of nested answers (11/54). The strict executor was valid on every strict call I counted (382/382).
BASE was unmodified src (hash stable across runs), arms were interleaved, and E2's archived reps came from the same src. No cases were dropped: Unresolved and ProviderFailure are counted as failures.

Luna VERB headword precision is high: 52/52 on E7's held-out and 59/62 on my harder probe, 97.4% pooled (CI 92.5-99.1%). Controls, rare strong verbs, typos, colloquial forms, Konjunktiv II of non-homographs and the kriegen recipient passive were all right.
The report correctly flags that NOUN/ADV/NUM proposals break corpus conventions and should stay off.
claimsThatDoNotHold: 'Precision holds out of sample' / 'VERB precision was 100%': out of sample it is about 95% on harder sentences. The wrong real-word homographs (mitführen, führen for fahren, abwägen) are systematic, and no guard catches them.

'0 wrong lemmas' as an expected production property for VERB: under the observed presence bias, a wrong proposal that differs from the joined text becomes a stored wrong Lemma. The live sets simply contained no wrong proposals.

'Wrong VERB lemmas go from 8-9 per 54 to 0' as an effect of intake proposals: most of those (inflected joined text accepted by jev) are fixed by E2's VERB guard alone, which ships in both plans. The unique gain from proposals is latency and fewer Unresolved.

'The misses measure corpus-vs-analysis membership disagreement, not coverage': in production those clicks get the proposal for the analysis target, and E7's own records show wrong, unscored proposals there (nahmen -> nehmen, Modalverb -> modalverb, zu -> zu, erhielt -> erhalten).
'The 4 separable misses in H are sah|ein and nahmen|teil': nahmen-teil was correct in H. The misses are sah-ein and hat-angenommen.
'Corpus contract pass rises from ~56% to ~83%' as a generalizable number: the VERB corpus is in-sample for the added prompt rules (recipient passive, modals, typos).
'E4 acceptance 92-97% under H' as evidence of proposal quality: this is circular, because H picks the proposal by construction.
'Click cost drops ~$0.0001' as a net saving: per-sentence intake cost outweighs it unless there are 2-3 or more VERB clicks per sentence.
verification.adjustedImpact:
For VERB clicks with a ready proposal, the latency win is real and large: grammar p50 goes from about 1.2-1.4 s to about 0.33-0.36 s, and the click-time Luna call is removed on about 98% of matched clicks.

Accuracy is roughly neutral to slightly positive against the fair baseline (BASE plus E2's VERB guard). Unresolved drops from 18 to 10 on held-out. The large wrong-lemma reduction is mostly the guard's doing.

Expected VERB lemma error under H is about the intake proposal's error rate. That is under about 1% on simple textbook sentences, and about 5% (CI 1.7-13%) on harder text with homographs and Konjunktiv II forms. Unlike today's path, those errors are stored as confident Lemmas that jev never questions, and they also become the emoji key.

Net cost probably rises: +$0.00021-0.00028 per sentence against a saving of about $0.0001 per VERB click.

ADJ, Idiom and Collocation remain unmeasured live.
verification.productionChangeSafety:
Only conditionally safe to ship for VERB, as a latency optimization, not as an accuracy fix. Minimum conditions:
1. Use strict json_schema, or flatten the schema, as the report says.
2. Ship E2's VERB guard regardless. It carries most of the accuracy gain on its own.
3. Do not offer a proposal whose target membership differs from the clicked target in a way that implies repair. For example, drop the proposal when a head-only target gets a particle-verb headword whose particle is not a member, or when a split head gets a bare verb while the particle target got the compound.
4. Given presence bias, treat an offered proposal as unverified. Ideally jev should judge it without an easy 'take the offered option' path, or the proposal should be accepted only when it agrees with jev's own hasSepPrefix and lexicallyReflexive judgments and the member surfaces. Even so, homograph errors (mitführen, fahren/führen, abwägen/abwiegen) will get through.
5. Keep the emoji key and the lemma decoupled, or accept that their errors become correlated.
6. Before widening to ADJ, Idiom or Collocation, rerun live with analysis targets once jev credits return, and measure BASE against H on a harder held-out set with homographs written by someone other than the prompt author, including what BASE does on the 3 homograph cases here.

Do not enable NOUN, ADV, NUM or PROPN proposals.

findings: Mechanism confirmed offline (results/legality-probe.json): a NOUN bag with number null is legal only when some other feature is set. The NOUN features call never asks article or case, so when jev answers Marked + Unmarked for a NOUN with no article evidence, the bag is all null. src rejects that with 'Feature Bag must contain a marked feature', which is the IncoherentApplicableFeatures failure.

IncoherentApplicableFeatures failures on NOUN eval dropped from 2/45 in each baseline rep to 0/45 in each variant rep. Number-field accuracy went from 41/44 to 44/44 in both reps (judged from jev answers), and from 34/34 to 35/35 in outputs. No arm produced a wrong output number.

Pass counts are flat at 25/45 in all four arms. In each variant rep there is +1 real rescue (vocative-leute, 2/2 reps) and -1 flip on a near-tied answer to the separate 'canonical' question. The resample shows that flip is noise: baseline 8/10 vs variant 7/10 over 5 samples per arm, with unchanged margins, and one baseline sample lost both cases.

The expected +1 pass gain on this corpus is too small to show above noise. The benefit is established case by case (same rescue in 2/2 reps, same result in E3's natural clicks, 3/3), not by the aggregate pass count.
Removing Unmarked never pushed jev from Unmarked to Unresolved for number (0 cases), so the no-fallback design costs nothing here.

Citation safety: on all 5 NOUN gold-null cases, inflection stays Citation in every sample and P(Marked) does not move. Because src ignores the number answer under Citation, the forced Sing never reaches the output.

PROPN is untouched: 0 edited requests, and replays are byte-identical to baseline. jev gave 0 Marked + Unmarked answers across 68 PROPN baseline samples, so there is no evidence for extending the change to PROPN.

Cost and latency: 17 fewer input tokens per NOUN features call; the Luna follow-up rate is unchanged (4/45). Median jev latency was 326 ms baseline vs 342-344 ms variant. That gap is not attributable: the distributions overlap heavily (the chance a variant call is slower than a baseline call is only 0.55-0.60), the request is shorter, and the variant ran later.

jev is stochastic on identical requests: about 33% of option probabilities differ, by 0.007 on average, and near-tied choices flip. NOUN noise here is low (0 outcome flips in 45 between b1 and b2), but near ties such as canonical margins of 0.02-0.10 flip freely.

Side finding outside E8's scope: accept-suspended-nonbreaking ('Kinder' written with the non-breaking hyphen U+2011) still fails after the number fix. The failure is in project.ts's suspended-completion check, the same one that fails suspended-hyphen-genitiv (U+2010) and oder-singular.
result.recommendedChange: Ship for NOUN only. In battery/dumgen/src/concrete-lang/de/grammatical-resolution/feature-questions.ts, change featureQuestion() so that when kind === "NOUN" and path === "surface.inflectionalFeatures.number", the null value is skipped and no Unmarked criterion is emitted. The question then offers Sing, Plur and Unresolved. No consumption change is needed in judgments.ts: Citation still gives a null inflection bag and the number answer is ignored, and no argmax fallback is required. Optionally reword the shared Unresolved criterion text, which mentions Unmarked, for this question. Do not extend the change to PROPN: there were no failures to rescue there. Separately, open a follow-up for the suspended-completion check in project.ts, which rejects 'Kinder' written with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011) or a Unicode hyphen (U+2010).
result.expectedProductionImpact: This removes the IncoherentApplicableFeatures failure class for contextual NOUNs: bare mass nouns such as Obst, Gemüse and Material, and plural-only nouns in direct address such as 'Hallo, Leute'. Those clicks currently produce no Attestation. It hit 2/45 NOUN corpus cases per run (4.4%) and 3/20 natural NOUN clicks in E3. Rescued clicks get the correct number (3/3 here, 3/3 in E3). One of the two corpus hits is still blocked by the separate suspended-hyphen bug. There are no extra calls, 17 fewer input tokens per NOUN grammar call, and no measurable change in latency or Luna follow-ups. - The change swaps a failure for a forced guess. If jev wrongly answers Marked on a citation-like NOUN, a Sing/Plur number now reaches the output where there used to be a failure. Observed P(Marked) on citation cases was at most 0.10, unchanged by the variant.

problems: The side finding is misdiagnosed. The suspended-completion failure is not specific to U+2010/U+2011 hyphens. Three cases with an ordinary ASCII hyphen fail with the same error in every arm: accept-suspended-dativ-plural, nominativ-plural and oder-singular. In all five failing suspended-left cases the direct cause is jev answering normalization_0 = Keep (P 0.92–0.97) instead of Generate. The normalized member therefore stays 'Kinder-' or 'Kinder‑', and project.ts's check (whose regex already accepts -, U+2010 and U+2011) correctly rejects a compound that was never completed. The recommended follow-up against project.ts's hyphen handling points at the wrong component.

One stated risk does not exist. 'A Marked NOUN with article evidence and number Unmarked is legal today' is wrong: judgments.ts always sets article and case to null in the NOUN bag before the legality parse. So Marked + number Unmarked is always illegal for a NOUN, whatever the article evidence. The change removes no legal outputs. This error is harmless and works in the change's favor.

The rescue evidence in the report is all in-sample. vocative-leute (corpus) and Obst/Gemüse/Material (E3 natural clicks, n=1 each) are the very cases that motivated the change. The experimenter's own probes are only safety probes, all cloned from the corpus template 'Wörterbucheintrag: X', and they are easy (P(Marked) at most 0.10). No held-out contextual rescue case was tested. My held-out check fills that gap, and it confirms the rescue.

A rescued click is not always fully correct. For 'Der Tisch ist aus Holz' the variant gets number Sing right in 3/3 samples but outputs case null instead of Dat. The NOUN case question keeps its own Unmarked option, and jev picks it (P 0.53–0.64) in 6/6 samples in both arms. The baseline hid this because the whole bag failed. The report's statement that rescued clicks get the correct number is true, but the rescued Attestation can lack a case that the preposition determines.

Removing Unmarked is not neutral in probability. Part of its mass moves to Unresolved: corpus mean P(Unresolved) roughly doubles, and on suspended-nonbreaking the margin over Unresolved is only 0.08. 'Never pushed to Unresolved (0 cases)' holds in all 90 corpus variant samples and 51 held-out variant samples, but 'costs nothing' rests on thin margins in the hardest cases. suspended-typo, whose baseline number answer was correct, now has Plur 0.51–0.58 against Unresolved 0.35–0.39.

The tested wording keeps references to the removed option: the NOUN question stem 'If this target has contextual nominal inflection...' and the Unresolved criterion '...do not use Unmarked for uncertainty'. The 'optional reword' in the recommendation was never tested. Given the migration toward Unresolved, a reword could shift those margins.

Minor statistical wording: the latency overlap is 0.556–0.63 rather than 0.55–0.60, and the mean probability difference of 0.007 is taken over all probabilities (0.021 among those that differ). Neither changes a conclusion.
Luna follow-ups were shared across arms through an exact-request tape. This is disclosed and fair, but Luna text quality was not sampled independently in either arm.

Nothing was dropped or silently failed: every arm has 84/84 records, no CapReached or Deferred, 50/50 NOUN requests sent Plur/Sing/Unresolved in the variant, and PROPN variant records are offline replays that would throw on a miss.
claimsThatHold: Mechanism: a NOUN Marked bag with number Unmarked is always all-null at the judgments.ts parse and fails with 'Feature Bag must contain a marked feature'. Confirmed both by the legality probe and by reading the code.

IncoherentApplicableFeatures failures on NOUN eval go from 2/45 per baseline rep to 0/45 per variant rep. Number judged correct goes from 41/44 to 44/44, and output numbers from 34/34 to 35/35, with 0 wrong numbers.

Held-out replication: baseline 5/39 incoherent failures vs variant 0/39. Every rescue gets the correct number (Sing for Holz, Geld and Brot). Contract-correct is 28/39 vs 30/39, and 0 wrong output numbers in either arm.

Pass counts are flat at 25/45. vocative-leute is rescued in 2/2 reps, and the other flip is noise on a near-tied canonical answer: the resample gives 8/10 vs 7/10, and the baseline sample nt-b3 lost both cases.
b1 vs b2 baseline noise is 0 outcome flips on NOUN eval. Reusing E3's tape for b1 does not create a selection effect, because the live b2 reproduces the same 2 failures.

Citation safety: inflection stays Citation and P(Marked) does not move on the 5 corpus/probe gold-null cases, or on my 3 harder metalinguistic mentions plus the ambiguous sign (12/12 samples per arm). The forced Sing never reaches the output.
In the observed samples, number was never answered Unresolved in the variant (0/90 corpus, 0/51 held-out).
PROPN is untouched: 0 edited requests, byte-identical replays, and 0 Marked + Unmarked answers in 68 samples. Nothing supports extending the change to PROPN.
Spend stayed under the cap ($0.029552 of $0.03). The variant sends 17 fewer input tokens per call, and the Luna follow-up rate is unchanged.
claimsThatDoNotHold: Side finding and follow-up: 'project.ts rejects Kinder written with U+2011/U+2010'. The same failure happens with ASCII hyphens (3 cases). The cause is jev choosing normalization Keep instead of Generate in all 5 suspended-left cases; project.ts correctly rejects the uncompleted member.

Risk item: 'a Marked NOUN with article evidence and number Unmarked is legal today, and that path is removed'. That path does not exist, because NOUN article and case are always null at the judgments.ts parse.
'Removing Unmarked costs nothing here' overstates the case. No argmax flipped, but P(Unresolved) rises systematically and the margin is as thin as 0.08 on the hardest corpus case.

Implied in 'rescued clicks get the correct number': that rescued outputs are correct. Held-out 'aus Holz' is rescued with the right number but case null instead of Dat in 3/3 variant samples, because the NOUN case question also offers Unmarked.

The expected production impact of 2/45 (4.4%) understates the failure class for bare mass nouns. On held-out bare contextual nouns the baseline failed 5/39 samples (13%), and several correct baseline answers sat at P(Unmarked) 0.3–0.45. The held-out cases were chosen to be risky, so treat this rate as an upper-range estimate rather than a production rate.
verification.adjustedImpact:
The change removes the IncoherentApplicableFeatures failure for contextual NOUNs, and that result holds on held-out cases. On 13 new bare, mass, plural-only and direct-address clicks, the baseline failed 5/39 samples (Holz 3/3, Geld 1/3, Brot 1/3); the variant failed 0/39. Every rescue got the correct number, and there were 0 wrong output numbers in either arm. Contract-correct rose from 28/39 to 30/39.

On the corpus the effect is still invisible in pass counts: +1/45, below near-tie noise. For bare mass nouns in real text the failure rate is higher than 4.4%, because several correct baseline answers sit at P(Unmarked) 0.3–0.45.

Rescues are not always complete. With a governing preposition ("aus Holz") the rescued output can carry case null instead of Dat, because the NOUN case question keeps its own Unmarked option.

There is no measurable cost in calls, tokens (17 fewer per call), Luna rate or citation handling. Some probability mass shifts to Unresolved, but no answer flipped in 141 variant samples.
verification.productionChangeSafety:
It is safe to ship for NOUN only, in exactly the form tested: in featureQuestion, skip the null value for kind NOUN and path surface.inflectionalFeatures.number, and keep the existing question stem and Unresolved text. judgments.ts needs no change.

What the tests show:
- **Wrong numbers:** 0 across 90 corpus variant samples and 51 held-out variant samples.
- **Citation and mentions:** unchanged (P(Marked) did not move, including harder metalinguistic uses with P(Marked) around 0.3).
- **PROPN:** unaffected.
- **Scope:** featureQuestion is also called for the NOUN case question in noun-article.ts, so the condition must stay specific to the number path.

What to watch or avoid:
- **Rewording:** do not reword the Unresolved criterion without re-testing. The removed Unmarked mass partly moves to Unresolved; the thinnest observed margin is 0.08, on suspended-nonbreaking.
- **Suspended-compound follow-up:** do not open it against project.ts's hyphen handling. In all 5 suspended-left failures the real cause is jev answering normalization_0 = Keep (P ≥ 0.92) instead of Generate, including for plain ASCII 'Kinder-'.
- **New follow-up:** the NOUN case question answers Unmarked after a governing preposition ("aus Holz" gives case null). The rescued Attestations will expose this.
